rule.sl:
**will be** + -ing (kratko **'ll be**, zanikano **won't be**) za to, kar bo ob nekem času v teku: **This time tomorrow I'll be walking on Helvellyn.** (Jutri ob tem času bom hodil{m:|f:a} po Helvellynu.) Vljudno vprašanje o načrtih: **Will you be using the van tomorrow?** Kar bo tako ali tako: **I'll be seeing Jack at the market, so I can tell him.**

Kako izbrati:
- kar misliš: **will**: **I think it'll rain.**
- kar se že vidi: **going to**: **Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.** Pogosto je oboje prav.
- kar si {m:načrtoval|f:načrtovala}: **going to**: **We're going to climb Helvellyn.**
- kar je dogovorjeno: sedanjik z -ing: **I'm seeing the doctor on Friday.**
- kar piše v voznem redu: sedanjik: **The bus leaves at nine.**
- kar se odločiš zdaj: **will**: **I'll help you.**
- za **if** in **when**: sedanjik: **When the bus comes, I'll call you.**
rule.de:
**will be** + -ing (kurz **'ll be**, verneint **won't be**) für das, was zu einer Zeit gerade läuft: **This time tomorrow I'll be walking on Helvellyn.** (Morgen um diese Zeit bin ich am Helvellyn unterwegs.) Höflich nach Plänen fragen: **Will you be using the van tomorrow?** Was sowieso geschieht: **I'll be seeing Jack at the market, so I can tell him.**

Wie du wählst:
- was du meinst: **will**: **I think it'll rain.**
- was man schon sieht: **going to**: **Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.** Oft geht beides.
- was du vorhast: **going to**: **We're going to climb Helvellyn.**
- was ausgemacht ist: Präsens mit -ing: **I'm seeing the doctor on Friday.**
- was im Fahrplan steht: Präsens: **The bus leaves at nine.**
- was du jetzt beschließt: **will**: **I'll help you.**
- nach **if** und **when**: Präsens: **When the bus comes, I'll call you.**
rule.it:
**will be** + -ing (breve **'ll be**, negativo **won't be**) per ciò che a una certa ora sarà in corso: **This time tomorrow I'll be walking on Helvellyn.** (Domani a quest'ora camminerò sull'Helvellyn.) Chiedere con garbo dei piani: **Will you be using the van tomorrow?** Ciò che succederà comunque: **I'll be seeing Jack at the market, so I can tell him.**

Come scegliere:
- ciò che pensi: **will**: **I think it'll rain.**
- ciò che si vede già: **going to**: **Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.** Spesso vanno bene tutti e due.
- ciò che hai in programma: **going to**: **We're going to climb Helvellyn.**
- ciò che è fissato: il presente con -ing: **I'm seeing the doctor on Friday.**
- ciò che dice l'orario: il presente: **The bus leaves at nine.**
- ciò che decidi adesso: **will**: **I'll help you.**
- dopo **if** e **when**: il presente: **When the bus comes, I'll call you.**
rule.en:
**will be** + -ing (short **'ll be**, no **won't be**) for what will be going on at a time: **This time tomorrow I'll be walking on Helvellyn.** To ask politely about plans: **Will you be using the van tomorrow?** For what will happen anyway: **I'll be seeing Jack at the market, so I can tell him.**

How to choose:
- what you think: **will**: **I think it'll rain.**
- what you can already see: **going to**: **Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.** Often both are right.
- what you have planned: **going to**: **We're going to climb Helvellyn.**
- what is arranged: the present with -ing: **I'm seeing the doctor on Friday.**
- what a timetable says: the present: **The bus leaves at nine.**
- what you decide now: **will**: **I'll help you.**
- after **if** and **when**: the present: **When the bus comes, I'll call you.**

tip.sl: 💡 Slovenščina reče *bom hodil{m:|f:a}* za oboje, angleščina loči: takrat v teku **I'll be walking**.
tip.de: 💡 Deutsch sagt oft das Präsens mit *morgen*, Englisch wählt: Fahrplan **leaves**, Plan **going to**, ausgemacht **I'm seeing**.
tip.it: 💡 L'italiano dice spesso il presente con *domani*, l'inglese sceglie: orario **leaves**, programma **going to**, fissato **I'm seeing**.
tip.en: 💡 Ask what is doing the telling: a timetable **leaves**, your plan **going to**, your thought **will**.
